links.comparator_used: Non-reasoning models (reasoning vs non-reasoning LLMs across 107 models)
links.outcome: Stigma rate in LLM-generated reasoning text
links.effect: Reasoning models 2.35% vs non-reasoning 1.70% stigma rate (p < 0.0001)
links.tradeoff: Reasoning-enhanced models produced more stigmatizing language, a new safety failure mode.
links.quote: Reasoning models showed higher stigma rates than non-reasoning models (2.35% vs. 1.70%; p < 0.0001), whereas medical models did not show significantly lower stigma rates than general-purpose models (1.80% vs. 2.00%; p = 0.26).

links.comparator_used: Standard prompt without destigmatizing prompt engineering
links.outcome: Stigma rate in LLM reasoning text and task performance
links.effect: Effect varied across models; stigma rates reduced by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance
links.quote: The effectiveness of prompt engineering as a destigmatizing approach varied across models, with stigma rates reduced by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance.
